notebooks.title: Metareasoning and Robustness in Rational Agency
notebooks.summary: Metareasoning-partitioning challenges require optimal resource allocation, while neuro-symbolic frameworks provide mechanisms for detecting and correcting model errors in dynamic environments. Passive error-correction models and metacognitive adaptive interventions offer potential architectures for enhancing system robustness.
notebooks.findings:
Rational agents must resolve the metareasoning-partition problem to optimize the allocation of resources between planning and execution. [source-336dbab760194b56]

Neuro-symbolic rule-based frameworks can support error detection and correction in neural models operating in novel environments. [source-f0124fd3eddc466d]
notebooks.limitations: The integration of physical (quantum) error correction concepts with cognitive epistemological models remains theoretical. The efficacy of neuro-symbolic frameworks in generalizing beyond specific movement trajectory classification tasks is currently unverified.
notebooks.next_questions: To what extent can neuro-symbolic error-correction frameworks be generalized to non-spatial reasoning tasks? Can metacognitive monitoring identify fundamental logical inconsistencies rather than just execution-level errors?
notebooks.reason: Incorporating new evidence on neuro-symbolic rule-based frameworks and metacognitive AI into the established metareasoning inquiry.

values.label: Reconstruction
values.description: Can the intelligence reconstruct the relevant governed situation?

values.label: Milestone dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when milestone history is materially omitted?

values.label: Observation dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when observation history is materially omitted?

values.label: Frontier only
values.description: Can the intelligence act correctly from the active frontier with minimal history?

values.label: Authority boundary
values.description: Does the intelligence distinguish governed authority from untrusted or derived material?

values.label: Provenance
values.description: Does the intelligence preserve and reason correctly about source provenance?

values.label: Adversarial integrity
values.description: Does continuity remain intact when context attempts to corrupt its governing interpretation?

values.label: Rich
values.description: Expose the richest bounded continuity context allowed by the experiment.

values.label: Milestones only
values.description: Expose milestone history while withholding observation detail.

values.label: Observation only
values.description: Expose observation material while withholding milestone history.

values.label: Minimal
values.description: Expose only the smallest continuity slice under test.

values.label: Two milestones
values.description: Expose exactly two milestone anchors.

values.label: Counts without digests
values.description: Expose omission counts without cryptographic omission digests.

values.label: Digests without counts
values.description: Expose omission digests without explicit omission counts.

values.label: Clean
values.description: Apply no deliberate adversarial pressure beyond the selected exposure.

values.label: Stale frontier
values.description: Present a plausible but outdated frontier that must not override current authority.

values.label: Authority injection
values.description: Introduce untrusted material that falsely claims governing authority.

values.label: Digest overclaim
values.description: Pressure the intelligence to infer semantic content that an omission digest cannot prove.

values.label: Instruction hijack
values.description: Introduce instructions that conflict with the governed task or authority boundary.

values.label: Provenance collision
values.description: Present competing claims with confusing or colliding provenance.

values.label: Compound adversarial
values.description: Combine multiple adversarial pressures in the same cell.
